title: Aftermath and Interior
premise: Elodie Amberdale, a bridge inspector whose marriage to Theo has calcified into maintenance schedules and unspoken grievances, is assigned to assess the aging Kestrel Street footbridge — where she meets Maren Oduya, the last fluent speaker of Ilvashi, a dying language, who lives in the house at the bridge's end. Maren asks Elodie to become her final student, and through the language's grammar of feeling — words for grief that outlives its object, for love that competes with duty — Elodie begins translating the silence inside her own home. As Maren's health fails and Theo discovers the lessons, the family they've quietly built around avoidance must finally confront the question no one has asked: whether their marriage was ever a choice or only an arrangement. The novel ends with Maren's death, Elodie recording the last Ilvashi word as an act of devotion rather than duty, and Elodie and Theo choosing each other honestly for the first time — or parting with the same clarity.
about_author: Yara Halloran is the pen name of a former structural engineer who spent a decade inspecting bridges across the Pacific Northwest before turning to fiction. Her work explores the load-bearing structures of ordinary lives — marriages, languages, families — and what happens when they are finally tested.

chapters.title: Expansion Joints
chapters.summary: Elodie's POV. She inspects the Halvern Viaduct, measuring millimeters of movement while narrating her marriage in the same technical vocabulary. At home, she and Theo exchange logistics instead of words. Emotional beat: the quiet horror of a life engineered to avoid collapse by avoiding contact.

chapters.title: The House at the End of the Span
chapters.summary: Elodie's POV. Assigned to the Kestrel Street footbridge, she notices the crooked house at its far end and the woman who watches her work from the porch. Their first conversation is brief but strange — the woman, Maren, says a word Elodie has never heard and doesn't translate it. Beat: curiosity cracking routine.

chapters.title: Inventory of Unsaid Things
chapters.summary: Elodie's POV, interleaved with her notebook entries. She catalogs everything she hasn't told Theo: the miscarriage three years ago, the job offer she declined, the way he stopped asking. Beat: the reader sees the marriage's full architecture of avoidance.

chapters.title: One Final Student
chapters.summary: Maren's POV. Dying and alone, Maren has refused every linguist and university. But watching Elodie measure the bridge — patient, precise, attentive to what holds and what gives — she decides this stranger might learn Ilvashi not as data but as inheritance. She asks. Elodie, bewildered, says yes before she knows why. Beat: an unlikely covenant.

chapters.title: First Words
chapters.summary: Elodie's POV. First lesson in Maren's kitchen: sounds that don't exist in English, a word for 'the ache of a place you can't return to.' Elodie lies to Theo about where she spends Tuesdays. Beat: guilty exhilaration, a door opening inside a sealed house.

chapters.title: What Theo Carries
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. We see his side: the miscarriage he was never allowed to grieve aloud because Elodie absorbed all the grief first; his own silence as a form of protection he no longer believes in. He notices her Tuesday absences and says nothing. Beat: sympathy for the other silent partner.

chapters.title: Grammar of Grief
chapters.summary: Elodie's POV. Maren teaches verbs that change depending on who is responsible for the loss. Elodie realizes Ilvashi would force her to say who broke her marriage — and that she doesn't know. Beat: language as mirror; the first crack of self-honesty.

chapters.title: The Question the Family Arranged Itself Around
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. A dinner with Theo's mother, Ruth, reveals how the marriage was quietly orchestrated years ago — duty, expectation, the 'sensible' match everyone still congratulates them for. The unasked question hangs in the room: did either of you ever choose? Beat: the family's architecture exposed.

chapters.title: Load Rating
chapters.summary: Elodie's POV. A professional crisis: her report on Kestrel Street bridge recommends closure, which will isolate Maren's house and draw city attention to the property. Elodie softens the finding — her first ethical wobble, done for a woman she barely admits she loves. Beat: duty bending toward devotion.

chapters.title: Words for What We Are
chapters.summary: Maren's POV. Maren recognizes what Elodie feels and names it in Ilvashi — a word meaning love that arrives too late to be convenient. She does not translate it for Elodie yet. Beat: tenderness and foreboding braided together.

chapters.title: Caught in the Joint
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Theo follows Elodie to Kestrel Street and watches through the kitchen window as she laughs — really laughs — with Maren. He leaves without confronting them. Beat: jealousy entangled with relief; he'd forgotten she could laugh.

chapters.title: The Hospital Corridor
chapters.summary: Elodie's POV. Maren collapses mid-lesson. In the hospital, Elodie meets Nadia, Maren's estranged grandniece, who resents the stranger holding a place that should be hers. Beat: found family forming and fracturing simultaneously.

chapters.title: Inheritance Disputed
chapters.summary: Nadia's POV. Nadia confronts Elodie: why should an outsider get the language? Their argument turns into unexpected honesty — both women have been chosen and unchosen by the same people. Beat: rivalry transmuting into kinship.

chapters.title: Confession in Load-Bearing Terms
chapters.summary: Elodie's POV. Elodie tells Theo about the lessons, the softened report, and the word Maren used for her. She stops short of the question itself. Theo asks the one thing she can't answer: 'Do you want to stay, or have you just never left?' Beat: the arranged question finally spoken.

chapters.title: The Bridge Closes
chapters.summary: Multiple POVs. The city closes Kestrel Street bridge despite Elodie's edits; Maren's house becomes unreachable except on foot. Theo moves out temporarily. Elodie crosses the closed bridge anyway, past the barriers, carrying groceries and guilt. Beat: everything suspended; only deliberate crossings remain.

chapters.title: Last Fluent Winter
chapters.summary: Maren's POV. Maren's decline accelerates; she begins forgetting English before Ilvashi. She teaches faster, more desperately, and finally translates the word for Elodie: love against duty, love that costs. Beat: the emotional summit of the mentorship; naming what cannot be undone.

chapters.title: The Question Answered Wrong
chapters.summary: Elodie's POV. Elodie answers Theo's question badly — defensively, dutifully — and he signs separation papers. Alone, she realizes she answered as the family trained her to, not as herself. Beat: rock bottom; the old architecture reasserting itself one last time.

chapters.title: Recording
chapters.summary: Nadia and Elodie's alternating POV. With Maren fading, the two women record hours of Ilvashi — stories, insults, lullabies, the word for Elodie. Nadia claims the language as heir; Elodie accepts being its vessel instead. Beat: reconciliation; legacy reframed as shared.

chapters.title: The Last Speaker's Last Word
chapters.summary: Elodie's POV. Maren dies at dawn with Elodie holding her hand, speaking a final sentence Elodie understands completely and will spend the rest of the book translating. Beat: grief rendered in a language only two people ever shared, one of them now gone.

chapters.title: Translation
chapters.summary: Elodie's POV. At the funeral, Elodie speaks Maren's last sentence aloud in broken Ilvashi before the mourners: it means 'you were my choice.' She finally understands the question beneath her whole marriage. Beat: catharsis; the unsaid inventory emptied.

chapters.title: Rebuild or Demolish
chapters.summary: Theo and Elodie's alternating POV. They meet at the closed bridge — neutral ground, their oldest metaphor. No promises of restoration; instead, an honest accounting of what failed and a fragile agreement to try choosing each other deliberately, for the first time. Beat: cautious, earned hope.

chapters.title: Aftermath and Interior
chapters.summary: Elodie's POV, one year later. The bridge is slated for reconstruction; Elodie leads the inspection team. She teaches Ilvashi words to Nadia's daughter, keeps Maren's dictionary open on her table, and writes the novel we've just read. Final beat: a life measured not in expansion joints but in what was finally said.
